flagged.evidence: The text says the endpoint cases “cannot be added to that existence statement.” Read literally, this is false for p=1: for any f in L^1 and bounded ball B, Tonelli gives integral_B integral K_alpha(x-y)|f(y)| dy dx = integral |f(y)| integral_B K_alpha(x-y) dx dy. The inner integral is uniformly bounded in y because |z|^(alpha-n) is locally integrable for alpha>0 and bounded on distant translates. Thus the absolute potential is finite almost everywhere on every bounded ball, hence almost everywhere on R^n. The p=1 counterexample refutes the strong L^1-to-L^{n/(n-alpha)} estimate, not the a.e. existence clause.
Step 1.1 defines theta=alpha p/n but asserts “theta q=alpha q/n.” For the valid parameters n=3, alpha=1, p=2, q=6, theta q=4 while alpha q/n=2. The identity should be theta q=alpha p q/n=q-p.

flagged.evidence: The proof says that for every y in B(0,r), K_alpha(x-y) >= (|x|+r)^(alpha-n). But the in-scope definition assigns K_alpha(0)=0; when x is in B(0,r) and y=x, the left side is 0 while the right side is positive. This singleton exception does not affect the integral lower bound, which holds almost everywhere, so the gap is nonfatal.
